name: lag.zoo
title: Lags and Differences of zoo Objects

origin.description: Shift a zoo series by observations.

arguments.name: k
arguments.text: Number of observations to shift. A positive k moves values to earlier indexes. A vector of lags is merged into columns.

arguments.name: na.pad
arguments.text: When TRUE, indexes dropped by the shift are put back with value NA.
Passed along when k has several values. A single lag ignores it.

origin.details: A positive k drops the first k values and the last k indexes, so each remaining value sits on an earlier time. A negative k does the opposite. k is rounded, with a warning when it was not an integer. If abs(k) is larger than the number of rows, k becomes that row count, so a large negative lag becomes positive and can return an empty series. na.pad = TRUE calls merge on an empty series with the original index and all = c(TRUE, FALSE). This R method does not call the C routine zoo_lag.
origin.example:
x <- zoo(c(10, 20, 30, 40), 1:4)
z <- lag(x, k = 1, na.pad = TRUE)
show <- function(v) paste(vapply(as.numeric(v), function(a) if (is.na(a)) "NA" else sprintf("%.16g", a), ""), collapse = " ")
cat(show(coredata(z)), "\n", sep = "")
cat(show(index(z)), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Shift a zoo series by observations.

arguments.name: k
arguments.text: Number of observations to shift. A positive k moves values to earlier indexes. A sequence of lags is merged into columns, named lag1, lag-1, and so on unless k is a dict.

arguments.name: na_pad
arguments.text: When True, indexes dropped by the shift are put back with NaN.

translation.details: A positive k drops the first k values and the last k indexes. A negative k does the opposite. k is rounded, with a warning when it was not an integer. If abs(k) is larger than the number of rows, k becomes that row count. na_pad=True calls merge_zoo on an empty series with the original index and all=[True, False].
translation.example:
import math
import numpy as np
from zoo.series import Zoo
from zoo.window import lag_zoo

def show(values):
    array = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    flat = array.reshape(-1, order="F") if array.ndim == 2 else array.reshape(-1)
    parts = []
    for value in flat:
        value = float(value)
        parts.append("NA" if math.isnan(value) else format(value, ".16g"))
    return " ".join(parts)

x = Zoo([10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0], [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0])
z = lag_zoo(x, k=1, na_pad=True)
print(show(z.data))
print(show(z.index))
